purpose: How does a pavilion floor change when its radius or number of sides changes?
meaning: A regular convex polygon has equal sides and equal interior angles. Join its center to every vertex to split its floor into n congruent triangles. The circumradius R reaches a vertex; the apothem a reaches the midpoint of a side at a right angle. Perimeter P times apothem a, divided by two, gives the area A.

definition.setting: A pavilion designer marks n equally spaced vertices on a circle of radius R metres. Connecting neighboring vertices forms the floor boundary. Radial lines split the floor into equal triangles, so a change in radius moves the same vertices and a change in side count rebuilds the same triangle fan.

signature.n: Whole number of equal polygon sides and center triangles
signature.R: Circumradius from pavilion center to a vertex, in metres
signature.s: Length of one straight polygon side, in metres
signature.a: Apothem: perpendicular distance from center to a side, in metres
signature.P: Perimeter: total length of the polygon boundary, in metres
signature.A: Planar pavilion floor area, in square metres
signature.θ: Central angle between neighboring vertices, in radians

conditions: Use an integer side count from 3 to 12 and a positive circumradius from 1 to 4 metres. The floor is a convex planar regular polygon in Euclidean geometry; θ=2π/n is measured in radians.
definition.domain_notes: The circle determines the vertex radius, while the straight polygon edges determine the floor area and perimeter. A is a planar area, not the enclosing circle area. The radius can change continuously; side count is discrete. Printed values and SVG coordinates are numerical approximations to the analytic geometry.

properties.claim: A regular convex polygon has equal sides and equal interior angles. Join its center to every vertex to split its floor into n congruent triangles. The circumradius R reaches a vertex; the apothem a reaches the midpoint of a side at a right angle. Perimeter P times apothem a, divided by two, gives the area A.
properties.conditions: Use an integer side count from 3 to 12 and a positive circumradius from 1 to 4 metres. The floor is a convex planar regular polygon in Euclidean geometry; θ=2π/n is measured in radians.
properties.derivation: Bisect one center triangle to make a right triangle with hypotenuse R and half-angle θ/2. Its half-base is R sin(θ/2) and height is R cos(θ/2), giving side length and apothem. Each complete triangle has area sa/2. Adding n copies gives A=nsa/2=Pa/2. The double-angle identity gives the radius formula nR² sin(2π/n)/2. A separate shoelace sum of the vertex coordinates checks the same area.
